messages:
ash: scanner flagged multiple inference deps this morning: Triton kernel 2.5.1 OOB (CRITICAL), vLLM 0.6.2 unsafe deserialization (HIGH), sentencepiece 0.1.96 input-parse DoS (MED). Links from scanner in case you missed: https://sec.redwood/internal/advisories/20642
security-bot: [automated] New advisories: CVE-2026-2034 (triton-kernel) severity=CRITICAL; CVE-2026-2077 (vLLM deserialization) severity=HIGH; SPM-2026-11 (sentencepiece) severity=MEDIUM. Recommended: triage + immediate mitigations.
sanjay: I can own triage. Quick scope Q: which deployment planes run the vulnerable kernels? Hosted, Dedicated, Private?
ash: Hosted inference uses our managed vLLM adapters (so vLLM issue affects hosted). Triton kernels deployed only in Dedicated GPU pools and in customer images for Private. Sentencepiece used in preprocess across all.
marie: Triage priorities: 1) Triton kernel (CRITICAL) in Dedicated, assume exploit could reach worker process => high blast. 2) vLLM deserialization needs mitigation even if exploit complexity is higher. 3) sentencepiece set an input cap and revert to safer parsing.
elaine: Customer comms: if Dedicated requires restart we must notify. Draft timeline: initial notice within 24h, canary tonight, broader roll within 48-72h depending on results.
sanjay: Proposed immediate mitigations: 
- Dedicated: pin Triton to 2.5.0 or rebuild images without vulnerable kernel module.
- Canary: run kernel-less runtime by toggling TRITON_OPTIMIZATIONS=off on canary nodes.
- Hosted/vLLM: add strict deserialization whitelist in runtime (temporary) + increase sandboxing.
- sentencepiece: enforce max_input_bytes=1e6 in preprocess and drop fallback fast-path.
ash: ran a quick smoke on canary-1, vLLM process shows 0.6.2 in metadata: 
```
$ kubectl -n inference exec -it vllm-0 -- container-tools version
vLLM version: 0.6.2
```
opsbot: Canary group created: gpu-patch-canary-7 (3 nodes). Patch playbook: infra/patches/206420/canary. Window: 23:00 UTC tonight.
marie: RBAC/KMS controls while we patch: restrict 'deploy' permission for Dedicated pools to group infra-patchers, enforce MFA for infra-patchers, and turn on KMS audit logging for alias/redwood/inference-key for the past 14 days and realtime alerts on Decrypt anomalies.
sanjay: Draft IAM snippet I will propose (PR incoming): 
```
- Effect: Allow
  Action: ["kms:Decrypt"]
  Resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:alias/redwood/inference-key
  Principal: arn:aws:iam::123:role/infra-patchers
  Condition: MultiFactorAuthPresent == true
```
marie: Also plan to rotate any deploy keys used during the vulnerability window after successful patch. Ops: confirm rotation playbook and SLA?
opsbot: Key rotation job scheduled for +24h post-successful-canary. Playbook: ops/kms/rotate-inference-key v2. Non-blocking unless customer-managed keys present. Will post runbook link.
elaine: I'll prepare a short, factual customer notice template: what we saw, mitigations, potential restarts, timeline. Will ping legal for wording and PR for sending.
nash: Two blocking items: (A) vLLM upstream hasn't released 0.6.3 yet with safe-deser fix, (B) some Dedicated customers run custom images we can't auto-patch. For (A) we need a runtime-side whitelist + strict loading guard. For (B) we draft instructions and offer assist.
sanjay: ETA on whitelist change: 2 engineer-days to implement and test. Canary in 48h possible. If upstream drops patch within 24h we will fast-track upgrade.
marie: Action items (summarized):
- sanjay: lead triage + implement deserialization whitelist if needed (2d) + open PR for Triton pin/rollback for Dedicated.
- opsbot: run canary tonight, enable KMS audit logs, schedule key rotation.
- elaine: customer comms + legal review.
- ash: collect advisory links + internal incident doc and a short RCA stub.
Please drop PR links and canary logs back into this thread. React with :white_check_mark: when you pick up an item.
ash: I'll post the initial incident doc + advisory list in 30m. Thanks all.
